items.subject: Grocery: Family Fare catalog is degrading - 1 signal(s)
evidence: COHORT IDENTITY: family-fare-regular-2026-08-01.json (final state, mtime 2026-08-01T22:06:26, 4706 rows) as_of histogram: 2026-07-18 x57, 07-25 x2, 07-26 x4, 07-30 x316, 07-31 x1008, 08-01 x3319. They are the LAST tranche of the 07-17..07-29 frozen-era backlog; the 24 expired at 2026-07-31T01:05 (ff-sweep-log) were the earlier tranche of the same drain.

Every term was successfully bought at least 3 times inside the 14-day carry window. Revisit period is roughly 10x shorter than the carry window: expiry here CANNOT be shard-rotation starvation.

THE PRODUCTS ARE MOSTLY STILL ON THE SHELF: Freshop /1/products/{id} probe (read-only, NOT the budgeted q= search endpoint) on 6 of the 55: pid 34710 Mc Cormick Chili Powder 2.5 Oz still available $3.49 (identical name and price); pid 1564405684713031798 was Chicken Breasts, Boneless & Skinless Fresh $3.99/lb, now Our Family Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast Family Pack $3.99 (RENAMED); pid 83739 was Minute Maid Orange Juice Carton 59 Fl Oz $5.49, now Minute Maid Minute Maid Low Pulp Original Orange Juice 59 Fl Oz $5.49 (RENAMED); pid 15421 was Pepperidge Farm Farmhouse Hearty White Bread, 24 Oz Loaf $4.99, now Pepperidge Farm(R) Hearty White Bread 24.000 Oz $4.99 (RENAMED); pid 458284 (Noosa Lemon 8oz) and pid 2313252 (Organic Avocados) return empty objects (delisted). The renamed successors are ALREADY in the merged catalog with as_of 07-31/08-01, so the catalog never lost those products - only their old NAMES, which a name-keyed carry can never refresh.

BOARD BLAST OF THE 55: pre-expiry board comparison-2026-07-31.json (built 2026-08-01T06:10): 0 of the 55 backed a crowned winner cell; 2 backed non-winner store entries: ground-coriander | Family Fare | Sugar N Spice Coriander Ground Pp | $2.09 / 2 oz | per-unit 1.045 (crown was Fareway Badia at 0.96) and turkey-bacon | Family Fare | Jennie O Turkey Bacon 12 Oz | $3.99 / 12 oz | per-unit 0.3325 (crown was Aldi Appleton Farms at 0.325). Post-expiry board (comparison-2026-08-01.json REBUILT 2026-08-02T07:44, i.e. built from the post-expiry FF file): ground-coriander keeps 4 stores, crown Fareway 0.96 unchanged; turkey-bacon keeps 5 stores, crown Aldi 0.325 unchanged. SECOND board checked (the recipe-board-blind-spot rule): board-price-overrides.json cells has 0 hits by item name and 0 by link_name. Total measured cost of the 55 expiries: two 15-day-old non-winner store entries, zero crowns moved, zero commodities dropped.

THE ONE REAL DEFECT FOUND (not what the alert claimed): ff-sweep-log 2026-08-02T07:00 run bought terms #458..#34 (686 rows collected), wrote the throttled diagnostic (out/throttled/family-fare-2026-08-02.throttled.json, mtime 07:06:40, deal_count 686), advanced the cursor #458 -> #35 (ff-term-cursor.json updated 07:06:40), then THREW Set-Content : The process cannot access the file at 07:06:41 (rc=1) on the MERGED file write: out/regular/family-fare-regular-2026-08-02.json mtime is still 06:18:38. A full window of purchases (686 rows of fresh prices and as_of re-verifications across ~104 terms) was silently discarded while the cursor advanced past those terms, so they wait a full ~1.2-day rotation for their next chance. Every merged-write failure repeats this. THIS is a mechanism that genuinely pushes rows toward the 14-day edge; the sharded sweep itself is healthy.

STEADY-STATE CHURN IS ARCHITECTURAL: the merged catalog is a NAME-KEYED UNION of every top-25 search response since 07-19 (4706 rows) while one full rotation currently yields ~3300-3900 unique names, so 800-1400 rows are always living on carry-forward. Renames, top-25 ranking drift, delistings, and the 2026-07-31 multi-buy skip all retire names without Family Fare losing the product. A nonzero trickle of 14-day expiries is therefore the HEALTHY steady state of this design, and the expired > 0 arm fires on it: it will re-fire around 08-09/08-10 when the 07-25/07-26 cohort (6 rows) ages out, and on every churn cohort after that.

surface_fix.what: Re-key the expiry arm of the Family Fare degradation alert from expired > 0 to STARVED expired > 0, where starved means the row's own search term has had no successful buy inside the carry window. Churn expiries (term recently successful, product simply no longer in its top-25 / renamed / delisted) are counted and logged but do not page. A mass-expiry safety net stays armed: total expiries above 2 percent of the merged catalog in one run still pages regardless of classification.
surface_fix.exact_change: (1) Ingest-Items gains a term parameter; every fresh row is stamped found_by_term (supplemental queries stamp the primary term). (2) Add found_by_term to the Norm-Row preserved-keys list so carried rows keep it. (3) Maintain out/ff-term-ledger.json: a map of term -> last date its query returned more than 0 items, merged with the prior ledger every run, written ONLY from measured receipt inside the buy loop (never bulk-stamped - the dates-written-not-measured trap). (4) At expiry time classify each expiring row via found_by_term against the ledger: starved (term last succeeded more than MaxCarryDays ago), churn (term succeeded recently), unknown (row predates the field). (5) Re-key Test-FfCatalogDegraded: signature becomes (mergedCount, prevMax, starvedExpired, churnExpired, recentVerified); fires on starvedExpired > 0, on starvedExpired+churnExpired > 2 percent of mergedCount, and keeps the recentVerified < 500 and 20-percent-shrink arms verbatim. Unknown-class rows NEVER page (paging on unknown recreates today's false page every day of the ledger warm-up); they are reported in the log line and fully disappear within 14 days as every carried row either refreshes or expires. (6) The alert body lists the starved TERM names, because a starved term is directly actionable (the F3 multi-term vocabulary path in commodity-search.json).

items.root_cause: Two mechanisms, neither of them Freshop misbehaving. (a) The 2026-07-31 re-key (plan item 30a1a8) gave the alert an expired > 0 arm on the belief that any 14-day expiry means the sweep cannot replace products. That premise is false for this architecture: the catalog is a name-keyed union of top-25 search responses, so store renames, ranking drift, delistings and the multi-buy skip guarantee a steady trickle of name-expiries while the store still sells the product - the arm conflates policy-expiry of union churn with sweep failure, because rows do not record which TERM found them and nothing tracks per-term last-success, so starvation (the only expiry that is real news) is unmeasurable. Today it fired on the final frozen-era cohort draining exactly on schedule, with zero board cost. It is the mirror of gates-that-can-never-arm: a trigger that at steady state can never stay false. (b) Separately, the pipeline DOES have one real slow-leak mechanism, found in this run's own logs: the merged-file write is not transactional with the cursor advance, so a write failure (a concurrent reader held the file at 07:06:41) discards an entire window of purchases while the cursor skips those terms for a full rotation.

root_fix.what: Make the merged write atomic and retried, and gate the cursor advance on the merged file actually landing, so no window of purchases can ever be silently discarded (this closes the only real degradation mechanism found). The per-term ledger from the surface fix is also the structural fix for (a): term starvation becomes a measured, directly-actionable signal instead of an inference from row ages.
root_fix.exact_change: (1) New helper Write-FfJsonAtomic(path, text): write to path + .tmp (a .tmp suffix does NOT match the *.json globs that scan out/regular, so a partial file can never be read as a store - same reasoning as the throttled-diagnostic relocation), then Move-Item -Force over the target, each step retried (5 attempts, 2s backoff) and non-throwing; returns true/false. Use it for the merged file AND the throttled diagnostic (whose bare Set-Content under EAP=Stop is the same class and sits BEFORE the merge). (2) Move the cursor-file WRITE to after a successful merged write; on failure log loudly, leave the cursor untouched (the next window re-buys the same slice, which is the correct no-loss behavior, identical to the existing cold-shutout rule), and exit nonzero so the sweep log shows it. Get-FfNextCursor stays pure and untouched; lift the commit decision into a pure helper, e.g. Get-FfCursorCommit(nextIdx, mergedOk) returning null unless mergedOk, so the self-test can REACH it - the 2026-07-29 reachability lesson. (3) Add a test-auditors.ps1 roster entry that runs pull-regular-familyfare.ps1 -SelfTest and asserts SELF-TEST PASS plus the presence of the new must-fire markers, so these fixtures run daily under the guard-fixture rule (today NOTHING in test-auditors executes this script's self-test).
root_fix.note_on_scope: A product_id-keyed carry merge (so a RENAME refreshes the row in place instead of expiring under the old name while the successor double-lives beside it) was considered and deliberately NOT included: measured on the 06:18 fresh window it would have removed 0 rows, its value drops to marginal once churn no longer pages, and it changes which NAMES exist in the matching corpus, which would drag a real routing measurement into an otherwise routing-neutral plan. If Brad wants the stale-price double-row risk closed later, it needs its own routing-measured plan item.

blast_radius.measured_by: No matching rule, engine branch, or corpus name changes ship in this item, so before/after routing is identical by construction for every product name in comparison-2026-08-01.json (rebuilt 2026-08-02T07:44), out/regular/*, out/sams, out/bakers and out/fareway. Verified concretely on the live pair: the fixes alter no existing row field that compare-deals reads (found_by_term is additive metadata) and remove no row; the atomic-write fix only PREVENTS future silent row loss, i.e. it keeps rows that are already the store's truth. Routing delta: zero names move.
blast_radius.risk: The only behavior deltas are: (a) a window whose merged write fails now retries and, if still failing, re-buys the same slice next window instead of losing it (strictly recovers data); (b) the alert stops paging on churn-class expiry - bounded by the untouched recentVerified and 20-percent-shrink arms, the new mass-expiry arm, and guard 9 freshness which still hard-fails the daily if the FF file stops advancing; (c) during the ledger 14-day warm-up, starvation on rows that predate found_by_term is not yet pageable (unknown class) - accepted and time-bounded, stated loudly here rather than smoothed over.

items.resolution_note: False degrading page, plus one real defect found in the same logs and fixed. The 55 expiries were the last 2026-07-18 frozen-era cohort draining exactly on schedule: the sharded sweep had re-bought every term 3+ times in the window (rotation ~1.2 days), 4 of 6 probed products are still on the shelf at unchanged prices (3 under NEW names whose successors the sweep had already captured), and the 55 backed zero crowns and zero commodities on either board (2 non-winner store entries, crowns unchanged). Re-keyed the expiry arm to measured term-starvation via found_by_term + out/ff-term-ledger.json with frozen must-fire/clean-twin fixtures now run daily by test-auditors. Also fixed: the 07:00 sweep lost a 686-row window when the merged write hit a file lock AFTER the cursor advanced - writes are now atomic and retried, and the cursor only advances once the merged file lands.
items.premise_verified: TRUE on every load-bearing premise, re-measured 2026-08-02 08:38-08:45 against files that had MOVED since the review (the freshness line predicted this and it happened: a local-daily run at 08:30 did a cold-shutout FF pull that rewrote family-fare-regular-2026-08-02.json at 08:32:31, fresh_count=0, carried_count=4655). What I checked, one by one. (1) THE 55: the 08-01 file (mtime 22:06:26, untouched, 4706 rows) has exactly 57 rows at as_of 2026-07-18; a name-keyed set difference against the current 08-02 file leaves 55, and the 2 survivors are 'Tomatillos' and 'Local Roots Organic Basil', both now as_of 2026-08-02. 57 - 2 = 55, exactly as the plan says. (2) AS_OF PROVENANCE: read at the source. Ingest-Items stamps as_of=$todayS at the moment Freshop answers and the carry loop reads $d.as_of from the prior row, so the 14-day arithmetic is measured, not builder-stamped. Confirmed. (3) ROTATION: ff-sweep-log cursor ranges 07-31 through 08-02 show 6-7 successful windows per day advancing ~82-104 terms each against a 527-term list, i.e. a full rotation in roughly a day, an order of magnitude inside the 14-day carry. Starvation is not the mechanism. Confirmed. (4) THE REAL DEFECT: confirmed in three independent places - ff-sweep-log 'THREW: Set-Content : The process cannot access the file' at 07:06:41 and 'sweep done rc=1 - cursor #458 -> #35'; ff-term-cursor.json mtime 07:06:40 holding next_index 35; and the merged file's mtime sitting at 06:18:38 until 08:32. The cursor certified a window whose rows never landed. (5) BOARD BLAST: re-ran it. Of the 55 names, 2 back a store row on comparison-2026-07-31 (ground-coriander 'Sugar N Spice Coriander Ground Pp', turkey-bacon 'Jennie O Turkey Bacon 12 Oz') and ZERO back a crown. On the post-expiry comparison-2026-08-01 (rebuilt 08-02T07:44) ground-coriander is 4 stores with the crown still Fareway 0.96 and turkey-bacon is 5 stores with the crown still Aldi 0.325; commodities_compared is 492 on both boards with no id present on one and missing on the other; board-price-overrides.json has 0 of 19 cells hit. Zero crowns moved, zero commodities lost. (6) THE .TMP CLAIM, which the plan asserted rather than measured, so I measured it: in a scratch dir, a sibling named family-fare-regular-<date>.json.tmp is invisible to all three glob forms this pipeline uses - Get-ChildItem 'family-fare-regular-*.json', Get-ChildItem '*.json', and Get-ChildItem -Filter '*.json' (the 8.3-short-name form, which was the real risk). The suffix is safe. ONE THING GROUND TRUTH CHANGED, recorded because the plan's do_not_touch depends on it: the orphaned 686-row diagnostic no longer exists. The 08:32 cold-shutout run overwrote out/throttled/family-fare-2026-08-02.throttled.json with its own deal_count=0, so 'do NOT hand-merge the 686 rows' is now moot rather than a temptation. Not a new class - it is the same non-transactional-write class the item fixes, seen one file over, and those terms come back on rotation as the plan said.
items.deviation: One file beyond the plan's declared set, one implementation choice, and one extra proof. (1) FILE: grocery/familyfare-sweep.ps1, two lines, additive. The plan's own fix creates a state that did not exist before - a cursor that sits still because the merged write failed, not because nothing was bought - and the sweep wrapper logs any unmoved cursor as 'sweep bought no terms ... hard shutout this window'. Shipping the fix without this would have made ff-sweep-log.txt assert something false on exactly the failure the item exists to catch, which is the conflated-log-line class that cost this pipeline thirteen days on 'throttled'. rc separates the two cases cleanly (a real shutout exits 0), so the shutout line is now gated on rc -eq 0 and a nonzero rc gets its own line saying the window was bought but not committed. No behaviour changes, no threshold moves, nothing else in the file is touched. (2) IMPLEMENTATION: the m4/c2 atomic-write fixtures call Write-FfJsonAtomic with BackoffSec 0 so a daily test-auditors run does not spend 8 seconds asleep. All five attempts, the non-throwing return, the byte-identity of the prior file and the tmp cleanup run exactly as they do live; only the sleep duration differs, and test-auditors pins the production defaults (Attempts = 5 / BackoffSec = 2) as a source check so they cannot be quietly dropped in the fixture's shadow. (3) PROOF: the plan's -SelfTest reaches the pure helpers but not the wiring, and the 2026-07-29 lesson is that unreachable is unshipped. I added a hermetic harness (scratchpad only, not committed) that runs the REAL script with -OutDir pointed at a scratch tree and -MaxMinutes 0, which makes Over-Cap true on the first loop iteration so zero q= search requests are spent and the Freshop budget is untouched. Against a frozen 4-row seed and a seeded ledger it drove the live path end to end: 1 starved / 1 churn / 1 unknown classified in the real carry loop, found_by_term preserved through Norm-Row on the carried row, the atomic merged write landed, the cold-shutout cursor stayed at #100, no .tmp orphans, rc=0, and the degraded branch reached with the alert correctly suppressed by its own stamp. The only line neither harness can reach without a live Freshop response is the fresh-row found_by_term stamp itself; that is pinned by source checks in test-auditors (call-site count, stamp present, Norm-Row preserves it) and will show up in tomorrow's sweep log per ship_sequence step 7.
